summary: The UK government says Norway follows Schengen area rules, and EU nationals have the right to travel freely there. Under Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 (consolidated to 30 December 2025), nationals of the countries in its Annex II, including the United States and the United Kingdom, are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period, and nationals of the countries in Annex I must hold a visa. Canada's travel advice says Svalbard, although Norwegian territory, is not part of the Schengen area.

defaultStayWindow.text: 90 days in any rolling 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area rather than per country. The day you arrive counts as the first day and the day you leave counts as the last. Leaving and coming back does not reset the allowance: on any given day, days already spent anywhere in the area during the preceding 180 still count against the 90.

fee.notes: Under the Schengen Visa Code as amended by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1415, children from six and below 12 pay EUR 45, and children under six are exempt.

European Commission (Migration and Home Affairs) — Applying for a Schengen visa

fee.text: Applicants shall pay a visa fee of EUR 90.

processing.text: That period may be extended up to a maximum of 45 calendar days in individual cases, notably when further scrutiny of the application is needed.

stayDays.text: This Regulation establishes the procedures and conditions for issuing visas for intended stays on the territory of the Member States not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period.

extendable.text: The period of validity and/or the duration of stay of an issued visa shall be extended where the competent authority of a Member State considers that a visa holder has provided proof of force majeure or humanitarian reasons preventing him from leaving the territory of the Member States before the expiry of the period of validity of or the duration of stay authorised by the visa. Such an extension shall be granted free of charge. 2. The period of validity and/or the duration of stay of an issued visa may be extended if the visa holder provides proof of serious personal reasons justifying the extension of the period of validity or the duration of stay.

name.text: Citizens of certain non-EU countries must hold a short-stay visa when travelling to the Schengen area.

method.text: An application shall be examined and decided on by the consulate of the competent Member State in whose jurisdiction the applicant legally resides.

passportValidity.text: The UK government tells British nationals that Norway follows Schengen area rules: their passport must have a date of issue less than 10 years before the date they arrive and an expiry date at least 3 months after the day they plan to leave the Schengen area.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Norway travel advice: entry requirements

travelInsurance.text: Under the Schengen Visa Code, visa applicants must hold travel medical insurance valid throughout the territory of the Member States and covering the entire period of the intended stay; the minimum coverage is EUR 30,000. No official source we could read states an insurance requirement for visa-exempt visitors.

source.name: Visa Code (Regulation (EC) No 810/2009), consolidated text — EUR-Lex

onwardTicket.text: No official source we could read states that a return or onward ticket is required. The UK government tells British travellers that at Norwegian border control they may need to show a return or onward ticket, proof of accommodation and proof of travel insurance, and prove they have enough money for their stay.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Norway travel advice: entry requirements

proofOfFunds.text: The European Commission's table of reference amounts says Norway assesses sufficient means on a case-by-case basis: NOK 300 per day with hosted or prepaid accommodation, NOK 1,300 per day without proof of accommodation, and at least NOK 1,000 per person per day when more than one person travels. The UK government tells British travellers they may need to prove they have enough money for their stay.

declarations.text: The UK Foreign Office says that when you travel into the Schengen area for short stays you may need to register your biometric details, such as fingerprints and a photo, that on your first visit you may be asked to do so at a special booth before the immigration desk, that there is no cost for EES registration, and that you do not need to take any action before you arrive at the border.

currencyLimits.text: Norwegian Customs says that if you are bringing currency with a value corresponding to more than NOK 25,000 to or from Norway, you must notify Norwegian Customs; the rule applies to Norwegian and foreign notes, coins and other means of payment.

source.name: Norwegian Customs (Tolletaten) — Currency

alsoStatedOn.name: Norwegian Customs (Tolletaten) — Alcohol and tobacco quotas

notes: Norwegian Customs says the alcohol quota is 1 litre of spirits, 1.5 litres of wine and 2 litres of beer, and that for tourists residing outside Norway the tobacco quota is 200 cigarettes or 250 grams of tobacco; you must be at least 18 to bring beer, wine and tobacco products and at least 20 for beverages over 22% alcohol.

Norwegian Customs says that if you bring more than the quota you must declare the amount that exceeds it, that the import of beverages with an alcohol content exceeding 60% is prohibited, and that new tobacco and nicotine products not approved in Norway, such as nicotine pouches and heated tobacco products, may not be imported.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says there is a small risk of petty theft, particularly at airports and railway stations in and around Oslo, and that terrorist attacks in Norway cannot be ruled out. Canada's travel advice says weather conditions can change rapidly, even in summer, and that in winter there is a risk of avalanches.

tips.text: Canada's travel advice says that while Svalbard is a Norwegian territory, it is not part of the Schengen area: you must have a valid passport to enter Svalbard and meet Schengen area entry regulations when returning to Norway's mainland.

Under Norway's Alcohol Act, drinks over 4.7% alcohol may be sold only by AS Vinmonopolet, whose shops may sell from 08:30 to 18:00 (10:00 to 16:00 on the day before a Sunday or public holiday). Drinks of up to 4.7% may be sold from 08:00 to 18:00, ending at 15:00 on the day before a Sunday or public holiday; the municipal council may restrict or extend these hours.

Canada's travel advice says Norway is prone to severe weather and the climate can be unpredictable at any time of year; it advises monitoring weather reports closely and says that in winter there is a risk of avalanches, some of which can be fatal.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Norway?
faq.answer: EU nationals have the right to travel freely in Norway. Under Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 (consolidated to 30 December 2025), nationals of the countries in its Annex II are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period, and nationals of the countries in Annex I must hold a visa. The UK government tells British nationals they can travel without a visa to the Schengen area, which includes Norway, for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Svalbard?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says Svalbard is Norwegian territory but not part of the Schengen area. You need a valid passport to enter it, and you must meet Schengen entry rules when you return to mainland Norway.

faq.question: Does time in Norway count toward the Schengen 90/180-day limit?
faq.answer: EU law describes Norway as a non-EU member of the Schengen area. The UK government tells British nationals they can travel without a visa to the Schengen area, which includes Norway, for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, and that visits to Schengen countries in the 180 days before you travel count towards your 90 days.

faq.question: How long can UK citizens stay in Norway?
faq.answer: The UK government says British nationals can travel without a visa to the Schengen area, which includes Norway, for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, and that the passport must have a date of issue less than 10 years before the date you arrive and an expiry date at least 3 months after the day you plan to leave the Schengen area.

faq.question: Do I need ETIAS to visit Norway?
faq.answer: The EU says an ETIAS travel authorisation will be an entry requirement for visa-exempt nationals travelling to any of the 30 European countries concerned, with a EUR 20 application fee, valid for up to three years or until the passport expires, whichever comes first. It says ETIAS is currently not in operation, no applications are collected, and the start date will be announced several months before launch. The official site is travel-europe.europa.eu.
